passage: I'm Mohit, and at sixteen I had to get myself across the city to a coaching class with nobody to drop me. The whole trip felt too big to solve, so I stopped trying to solve it. I asked only: how do I reach the bus stop? That was easy, ten minutes on foot. Next question: which bus? A neighbour's sister told me the number 47 goes past the centre. Third: the fare. I checked with the conductor and put two coins aside every day for a week. Each piece was small enough to fix alone, and stacked together they made a route. I gave my mother the route and my arrival time. On Monday I took the 47, arrived ten minutes early, and felt taller than I had in weeks.

qa.q: Which bus goes past the coaching centre?
qa.a: The number 47 goes past the centre.

qa.q: How did Mohit feel on arriving early?
qa.a: Mohit felt taller, meaning proud and more confident, after solving the trip piece by piece.

qa.q: What other approach could Mohit use to make the journey easier?
qa.a: Mohit could ask a classmate from the centre to travel together on some days, since company makes a long journey safer and simpler.

qa.q: How might Mohit's mother see the plan?
qa.a: Mohit's mother was probably reassured by having the route and arrival time, and glad Mohit had thought it through.

grounding: Shows a student who cannot get a lift to a coaching centre and breaks the trip into subgoals: reaching the bus stop, finding the bus number and arranging the fare.

passage:
Coaching centre note, Saturday 5 p.m.
Irawati was on time for the physics mock today, which surprised me. Her mother usually drops her, and I knew her mother was out of town this week.
At the break I asked how she got here. She explained it like a physics problem. "Getting across town felt impossible, so I broke it up. First, how to reach the main road bus stop. That's a ten-minute walk, fine. Then which bus. I asked the shop uncle and he said 42 goes near here. Then the fare. I checked I had coins."
She said none of the steps was hard on its own. Only the whole thing looked scary.
I've written the bus number and route on the centre's notice board for others without a lift.
— Gautam, physics faculty

qa.q: Which bus did the shop uncle say goes near the centre?
How did Irawati feel about the trip before breaking it up?
qa.a: Irawati felt the whole trip across town was scary and impossible at first, then less worried once each step was solvable on its own.

qa.q: What else could Irawati plan for the trip home, and why?
qa.a: She could note the last bus time and keep a phone number to call, so a missed bus doesn't leave her stuck.

qa.q: How might other students without a lift benefit from the note on the board?
qa.a: They can use the bus number and route that Irawati worked out, so the trip feels less daunting for them too.

grounding: It shows a teenager who has no lift breaking a trip across town into subgoals: reaching the bus stop, finding the bus number and having the fare.

passage:
Monday night
Big day. Papa's scooter broke down this morning and he said, sorry, no lift to coaching. My test was at four, across the whole city.
For ten minutes I just panicked. Then I remembered Sudha Ma'am saying, when a sum looks too big, split it.
So I did. Problem one: get to a bus stop. The one near the temple, fifteen minutes' walk. Solved. Problem two: which bus? I messaged my classmate Neha, she said 18A, then change to 7 at the market. Solved. Problem three: money. I had forty rupees in my pencil pouch. Enough. Solved.
It took an hour and ten minutes. I reached at 3.52, sweaty but there.
Sudha Ma'am saw me and smiled. I didn't tell her how scared I'd been.
Payal

qa.q: How long did the trip to coaching take?
qa.a: It took an hour and ten minutes.

qa.q: How can you tell Payal was scared when the lift fell through?
qa.a: Payal says the first ten minutes were spent just panicking, and later admits not telling Sudha Ma'am how scared it had felt.

qa.q: What else could Payal do before the next coaching day?
qa.a: Payal could write down the bus route and keep fare aside in advance, so a missed lift is not a panic next time.

qa.q: How might Sudha Ma'am see Payal arriving at 3.52?
qa.a: She sees a student who made it on time and is pleased, without knowing how hard it was, which is why she only smiles.

grounding: It shows a teenager with no lift breaking a trip across town into small subgoals: the stop, the bus numbers and the fare.
